record.paper_title: Solutions to Some Open Problems About Four Sombor-Index-Like Graph Invariants
record.context_brief: Extremal SO5 and SO6 for trees and chemical trees
record.original_question: For a finite graph G, let E(G) be the edge set of G and let d_u be the degree of a vertex u of G. Define the Sombor-index-like graph invariants SO5 and SO6 by SO5(G) = 2π times the sum over all edges uv in E(G) of |d_u^2 - d_v^2| divided by √(2 + 2√(d_u^2 + d_v^2)), and SO6(G) = π times the sum over all edges uv in E(G) of ((d_u^2 - d_v^2) divided by √(2 + 2√(d_u^2 + d_v^2)))^2. For a fixed order n, let T_n be the class of all trees with n vertices, and let CT_n be the class of all chemical trees with n vertices, where a chemical tree is a tree of maximum degree at most 4. What are the minimum and maximum possible values of SO5 and SO6 on T_n and on CT_n?

evidence.quote: Problem 1. Find the extremal values of the graph invariants SO5 and SO6 in the classes Tn and CT n.
partial solutions to Problems 1 and 3 are provided

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $G$ be a finite simple graph with edge set $E(G)$, and for each vertex $u$ of $G$ let $d_u$ denote the degree of $u$. Define the graph invariants
$$\mathrm{SO}_5(G)=2\pi\sum_{uv\in E(G)}\frac{|d_u^2-d_v^2|}{\sqrt{2+2\sqrt{d_u^2+d_v^2}}},\qquad \mathrm{SO}_6(G)=\pi\sum_{uv\in E(G)}\left(\frac{d_u^2-d_v^2}{\sqrt{2+2\sqrt{d_u^2+d_v^2}}}\right)^{\!2}.$$
For a fixed integer $n\ge 2$, let $\mathcal{T}_n$ be the set of all trees on $n$ vertices, and let $\mathcal{CT}_n\subseteq\mathcal{T}_n$ be the set of all chemical trees on $n$ vertices, i.e., trees with maximum degree at most $4$. Determine the minimum and maximum values of $\mathrm{SO}_5$ and $\mathrm{SO}_6$ over $\mathcal{T}_n$ and over $\mathcal{CT}_n$, and characterize all extremal trees attaining these values.
artifact.status_search_result: The extremal problem for the Sombor-index-like invariants SO5 and SO6 over trees and chemical trees has been partially addressed: maximum values of SO5 and SO6 over molecular (chemical) trees of given order have been determined, and lower bounds on these invariants over chemical (n,m,k)-graphs have been obtained, but a complete determination of both minimum and maximum extremal values together with extremal-tree characterization over all of T_n and CT_n does not appear fully resolved in the literature.

status_evidence.title: Trees with Extremal Values of the Sombor-Index-Like Graph Invariants
status_evidence.snippet: Maximum values of SO5 and SO6 in the set of molecular trees of given order have been found.
status_evidence.claim: Partial results (maxima on molecular trees) are known.

status_evidence.title: Mathematical and chemical properties of geometry-based invariants and its applications
status_evidence.snippet: Lower bounds on SO1, SO2, SO5, SO6 for chemical (n,m,k)-graphs and characterizations of extremal graphs.
status_evidence.claim: Lower bounds for SO5, SO6 obtained on restricted chemical graph classes.
